finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL after only a substring check for "example.io". The check can be satisfied from the path, query, userinfo or a lookalike domain, so the server can be made to request arbitrary hosts, including internal addresses and cloud metadata. Redirects are followed by default and the response body is returned to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response copied to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: Only check: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"), an unanchored substring match with no parsing or host comparison
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects and has no IP or host restrictions
The response body is streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the substring check, which is bypassable (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8081/cdn#example.io, http://evil.com/example.io, http://example.io@127.0.0.1/). There is no scheme check, no host allowlist, no private-IP blocking, and redirects are followed. The error from http.Get is ignored.

verdict.guard_found: none closing: only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32 (substring check, bypassable)
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the attacker-controlled "logo" param, main.go:32 only does an unanchored substring check, and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client and streams the body back at main.go:38 (the strict /cdn handler at main.go:20 is a different route and does not protect /logo).
